summary: A 100-foot MC-39 Aermotor with a 7x7 ft cab, built for the Alabama Forestry Commission in 1957 or 1958; the register gives both years.

facts.design: 100-foot MC-39 Aermotor with a 7x7 ft cab

events.note: Register's Built field gives 1958; its description says constructed in 1957 by a private contractor
Registered January 18, 2010 on nomination by Thomas Kaufmann

evidence.supports: constructed in 1957 by a private contractor for the Alabama Forestry Commission
evidence.quote: constructed in 1957 by a private contractor for the Alabama Forestry Commission

evidence.supports: tower described as 100-foot MC-39 Aermotor with a 7x7 cab
evidence.quote: It is a 100' MC-39 Aermotor with a 7'x7' cab.

evidence.supports: one of the last lookouts built in the state
evidence.quote: One of the last lookouts built in the state

evidence.supports: description spells the hill Saunders Hill
MC-39 was the most common steel lookout tower model in Alabama
evidence.quote: The most common steel lookout tower model in Alabama’s forests was the Aermotor MC-39, followed by the LS-40 version.

evidence.supports: probably fewer than 75 historic lookouts still standing in Alabama
evidence.quote: Today, however, there are probably less than 75 of these historic structures still standing in Alabama.

evidence.supports: many are very unsafe and illegal to climb
evidence.quote: Many are looking worse for the wear, are very unsafe, and are illegal to climb.

sources.title: Thomas Kaufmann: Keeping Alabama's historic lookout towers

notes_for_editor: The register gives 1958 in its Built field but says in its description that the tower was constructed in 1957; the record keeps 1958 and the story reports both dates. No correction proposed. The description spells the hill Saunders; the heading and record say Sanders. height_m 30.5 is the register's 100-foot figure, not confirmed as cab floor. The register does not state status or condition; the record's 'standing' is unconfirmed. No staffing, fire or access sources found. Two web searches found nothing naming this tower.
